rationale: The paper is a full-text mixed-methods case study combining quantitative financial modeling and budgetary/balance-sheet analysis (IRR cash-flow projections across the four concession blocks, Siafi-RJ grant allocation tracking, and Cedae operational revenue trends) with qualitative documentary and sociopolitical analysis of concession contracts, legislative committees, and public forums. The central mechanism analyzed is the 2020-2021 PPP/private concession of retail water and sanitation services in the State of Rio de Janeiro under Brazil's 2020 sanitation regulatory framework (regulatory_model_ownership). Secondary mechanisms examined within the concession design include multi-scalar metropolitan governance and fiscal recovery arrangements (institutional_structure_coordination), wholesale water tariff caps/margin-squeeze and grant-revenue diversion away from cross-subsidies (fees_tariffs_subsidies), contractual clauses exempting concessionaires from upgrading informal settlements ('áreas irregulares') lacking prior land-tenure regularization and urban infrastructure (eligibility_status_documentation), and the exclusion of social participation from governance bodies (participation_assistance). Empirically, the study evaluates institutional, fiscal, regulatory, and urban-metropolitan planning governance intermediate outcomes (administrative_outcome)—such as public rent capture, diversion of 67% of state grant proceeds to general payroll/administration, halving of Cedae's operational revenues, and contractual risk-shifting/omissions of metropolitan favelas that create uncertainty around future universalization promises—rather than measuring realized post-concession household connection or service-delivery changes.
